title: Satisfying every published Delegate requirement creates no entitlement to be accepted
content:
A.6.1.1.2.3.1.4.4.2.6 is unusually explicit: "Submission of a Delegate Application does not guarantee acceptance. Acceptance is at the Grove Foundation's **sole discretion**. The Grove Foundation may approve or deny any application at any time, **for any reason or no stated reason** including legal, sanctions, risk, operational, or capacity considerations **even if the applicant satisfies the minimum requirements**. The Grove Foundation is not required to provide individualized rationale. Decisions are final unless otherwise provided in this Artifact."

The clause exists to sever a link a reader would otherwise assume. A framework that publishes application requirements (A.6.1.1.2.3.1.4.4.2) invites the inference that meeting them earns admission. This says the requirements are a floor for consideration, not a specification of who gets in.

There are defensible reasons to write it this way. Published criteria are gameable: an actor who knows the exact test can construct an applicant that passes it while being exactly the participant the test was meant to exclude. Discretion also permits refusals that cannot be safely explained — a sanctions concern, a suspected undisclosed affiliation — where stating the reason would tip off the applicant or create legal exposure. And "capacity considerations" concedes plainly that the roster has a size, so some qualified applicants must be turned away.

The cost is that the only accountability mechanism left is reputational. There is no appeal, no reasons requirement, and therefore no way for an observer to distinguish a refusal on sanctions grounds from a refusal of someone likely to vote inconveniently. Since only Active Delegates may hold delegated voting power, this is discretionary control over the composition of Grove's most influential electorate.

A.6.1.1.2.3.1.4.9 supplies the one real constraint: Grove may amend the Delegation Framework "subject to the established Grove Artifact governance procedures related to Artifact edits." The discretion is unreviewable in application but the rule granting it is amendable through governance — so the check on the Foundation is the power to rewrite its mandate, not to overturn its decisions.
description: The Grove Foundation may deny any application for any reason or no stated reason even where minimum requirements are met, owes no individualized rationale, and its decisions are final.
